articles.title: US sanctions 10 entities for allegedly supporting Iran’s military
articles.summary: Individuals and firms in China, Pakistan, Turkiye, Iran and Saudi Arabia sanctioned as part of a pressure campaign.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump’s administration has added a group of 10 individuals and companies to its list of global entities being sanctioned over alleged ties to the Iranian military.

In a statement on Tuesday, the US Treasury accused representatives and technology firms based in China, Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia of procuring weapons and parts for Iran’s military. Three of the sanctioned entities were located in Iran.

“Today’s action further degrades the Iranian regime’s ability to reconstitute its weapons programs and increases the costs for those who choose to aid Tehran’s military procurement efforts,” the US Treasury said.

The sanctions were undertaken as part of Operation Economic Outcast, a Treasury Department effort to further restrict Iran’s access to global markets.

Iran has been locked in a war with the US and Israel since February 28, after the two allies launched a series of deadly attacks targeting Tehran’s leadership and military.

But critics have argued that the war has no clear end in sight, despite claims of victory on both sides.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Operation Economic Outcast in August, aimed at pressuring Tehran into agreeing to a deal to end the war.

Trump claimed the operation would usher in “economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale”, and he warned that any country that participates in trade with Iran would face “tremendous” consequences.

As part of the campaign’s initial volley of sanctions, China-based firms and business leaders were targeted.

But China remains one of Iran’s largest trading partners, and the Trump administration has faced scrutiny over how forcefully it would confront Beijing over its participation in Iran’s economy.

At the time, Bessent defended the administration’s decision to delay certain sanctions by saying, “We’re giving everyone the opportunity to remedy bad behaviour. Why would I want to blow up the global financial system?”

Trump recently hosted Chinese President Xi Jinping for his first state visit to the White House in more than a decade, after which Trump touted progress in the trade talks between the two countries.

Despite the warming ties, several Chinese firms were among those sanctioned in Tuesday’s announcement.

They included the Hong Kong-based company EC Mojo Technology Co Ltd, as well as one of its representatives, Li Fen.

EC Mojo had “provided electronic components” to the Iranian military, while Li “attempted to evade sanctions and export controls”, Treasury claimed.

Another designated firm was Saudi-based Cavalier Dynamics for Technologies Company. As part of its announcement, the US Treasury said it would take action “in coordination with Saudi government partners”.

All those included in Tuesday’s sanctions were allegedly involved in procuring “weapons and weapons components for Iran’s Ministry of Defense and Armed Forces Logistics (MODAFL), the entity responsible for weapons research, production and acquisition for Iran’s armed forces”.

Operation Economic Outcast has also sanctioned Iranian economic sectors not directly tied to its military.

Recent sanctions on the civilian airline sector have left some passengers stranded, after some Iranian airlines and international carriers suddenly cancelled flights to and from Iran.

But experts have questioned how effective the heightened sanctions campaign may ultimately be. Iran has faced heavy US sanctions for years, though on Tuesday its currency fell to a record low, amid war-related pressures.

articles.title: Morocco’s king appoints first woman prime minister following election
articles.summary: King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri on Tuesday as Morocco’s first woman prime minister after her liberal-centrist party came out on top in a September 23 parliamentary election, the royal palace said.
articles.body: King Mohammed VI appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri on Tuesday as Morocco’s first woman prime minister after her liberal-centrist party came out on top in a September 23 parliamentary election, the royal palace said. The king asked El Mansouri to form a new government, the palace said in a statement. El Mansouri’s Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM) was created in 2008 by an adviser to the king and has since positioned itself as a counterweight to the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD) by advocating social modernisation and secular-leaning views. Morocco is a constitutional monarchy where the king retains sweeping powers over foreign policy, defence and other key portfolios. Under Morocco’s constitution, the king appoints the head of government from the political party that wins the largest number of seats in the House of Representatives. PAM, which was ⁠the second-largest member in the outgoing coalition, moved up to the top spot, bolstered by the recruitment of Fouzi Lekjaa, Morocco’s football federation chief and two-time government budget manager, who joined weeks before the vote. El Mansouri, a lawyer who was housing minister in the outgoing government and Marrakech mayor, will lead talks to form a coalition government and submit a list of cabinet members for the king’s approval. ‘No red lines’ The incoming government will oversee the last stages of a $20-billion push to get ready for the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host with Portugal and Spain. It will also implement economic policies aimed at addressing widespread youth discontent, an issue highlighted by a mass border rush on the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July and deadly Gen-Z-led protests last year. PAM won 97 seats, followed by its partners in the outgoing government, the liberal-centrist National Rally of Independents (RNI) with 66 seats, and the conservative nationalist Istiqlal with 65. During the campaign, PAM had ruled out staying in a coalition with the RNI — the two had traded blame over policy shortcomings including a failure to halt rises in food prices. But El Mansouri said on Thursday she would have no “red lines” when it came to negotiations. “We have turned the page,” she said. Abdelilah Benkirane, former prime minister and leader of the PJD, which won 54 seats, said the party would stay in opposition. Three leftist parties took smaller shares of the seats. Turnout, closely watched as an indicator of trust in elected institutions, fell to about 38% from around 50% in the previous elections five years ago, when the moderate Islamist PJD was dealt a crushing defeat after a decade in power. In recent years, King Mohammed VI had appointed a female adviser and Morocco has had women in senior institutional roles. The outgoing government had four women ministers.

images.caption: Member of the collective leadership of Morocco's Authenticity and Modernity Party (PAM), Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, who is also Morocco's Minister of National Planning, Urban Planning, Housing and Urban Policy and Mayor of Marrakesh, speaks during a press conference at the PAM headquarters in Rabat following the announcement of the provisional results of Morocco's legislative elections on September 24, 2026.

articles.title: Spain protests: Evicted 87-year-old woman to return to Madrid home
articles.summary: The real estate firm backs down and restores her old rent after mass protests over Spain’s housing crisis.
articles.body:
Large protests have erupted in Spain over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman who is set to return to her Madrid home, her representatives said.

The lawyer representing Maria del Carmen Abascal, known across Spain as Maricarmen, said on Tuesday that the real estate firm offered to reduce her rent back to its pre-dispute rate.

Under the deal, her monthly payments would be capped at about $570 for the next eight years, taking up roughly 30 percent of her pension.

This is the latest development in an ongoing saga that started with her eviction last week.

Maricarmen became the face of Spain’s deepening housing crisis after an international investment fund bought her building and hiked her rent by more than 200 percent to roughly $1,880 a month, a move aimed at pushing out the long-term tenant to make way for lucrative tourist apartments.

Madrid’s tenants’ union organised protests and encampments in Madrid’s central Puerta del Sol square, drawing tens of thousands of demonstrators before spreading to dozens of other cities.

Upon the announcement of the landlord’s offer, the union celebrated what it described as a “historic win” in a post on X.

The government of Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez responded to the outcry by presenting a package of measures scheduled for a parliamentary vote this Friday.

The proposal most likely to secure approval extends expired tenant safeguards through 2030, shielding vulnerable residents like Abascal from eviction over that period.

The package falls short of the protesters’ demands and is likely to face opposition from conservative parties more sympathetic to landlords’ interests.

According to Spain’s central bank, the country is roughly 755,000 homes short of demand, a gap that could widen to a million units by 2028.

articles.title: Oldest known house built in Reno was sold for $1 on one condition: it had to be moved and preserved; in 2025, the 1868 Benham-Belz House was relocated after more than 150 years
articles.summary: The Benham-Belz House, which is believed to be the oldest surviving house built in Reno, sat at 347 West Street, on Lot 8 of Block E of the original Reno
articles.body: The Benham-Belz House, which is believed to be the oldest surviving house built in Reno, sat at 347 West Street, on Lot 8 of Block E of the original Reno townsite, for 150 years. But in July 2025, the historic house left the neighbourhood where it had stood since the 19th century. Its move was not the end of the house’s story, but an effort to preserve it. The historic house has been relocated to a private site near Mayberry Drive and McCarran Boulevard, just as its previous owner wanted. In spring 2024, it was sold to a private party for just $1, with one important condition: it had to be moved and preserved. More than a year later, on 10 July 2025, the house was relocated.Built in the year Reno’s history beganReno was barely a town when the house went up. The Central Pacific Railroad began selling lots on the original townsite in May 1868, and the family of I.T. Benham, a stonemason, bought Lot 8 of Block E, according to the Historic Reno Preservation Society (HRPS). The lot is now 347 West Street. The Benham-Belz House was constructed in Reno’s founding year, 1868, or early 1869, according to Reno Historical. No wonder it is the oldest surviving house constructed in Reno. That claim leaves out houses moved to Reno from elsewhere and ranch houses that stood outside town.The Benham family purchased the lot for $200, and the deed of sale was initiated on 4 June 1868, less than a month after Reno’s original land auction. The property was sold by Charles Crocker of the Central Pacific Railroad to Linda Benham, the wife of I.T. Benham, who was also named in the deed.Benham became a builder and contractor. He became one of Reno’s founding builders. HRPS credits him with the Central School, built in 1879 and 1880, a block north of his house. The building later became Reno’s first high school.Around 1880, the Benhams moved to Spokane. Later, in 1883, Reno barber John Belz bought the house, and the Belz family stayed for almost a century. Over the years, Belz became a popular barber in the city. His business was reportedly the first establishment in Reno to install electric lights, another small detail connecting the house and its occupants to the city’s development. When Belz died suddenly of heart failure in 1900, newspapers described him as a man of generous nature, good impulses and steady character. His death was mourned across the city. His daughter Florence lived in the house until her death in 1981 at the age of 87.Over the years, the house underwent many changes. By the time Florence passed away, the house looked different from the one Benham built. Historic photographs show that brick veneer was later applied over the original wood exterior.Sold for $1, but with a conditionAt one point, the house’s future remained uncertain. So, in early 2024, Jacobs Entertainment, the developer behind the Reno Neon Line District, bought the house for $1.2 million, according to local reports. The company’s CEO, Jeff Jacobs, said publicly that he would sell it for $1 to anyone willing to relocate it. The idea was to preserve and maintain it. There were many bids, of course. Jacobs picked Logan and Angelina Needham, a Reno couple, after what the company described as a thorough vetting process. For Jacobs, preserving historic homes mattered as the company reshaped downtown. The sale was announced a few months after the purchase. The move was first expected in the second half of 2024. But it didn’t happen until about a year later.On the morning of the move, the crew dismantled the house into two sections. Two large trailers took the halves to their new location. The new destination was a private site several miles west of downtown. Photos from the day show the two halves on their trailers and the rubble left behind on West Street.According to Needham, a custom steel fabricator, the house has to be brought up to code, which means grounded outlets and non-lead pipes, along with other appearance-related improvements. And now, after more than 150 years on the original Reno townsite, the house sits on a new site.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Life in the UK's mobile phone signal 'blackspots'
articles.summary: Most of the UK has access to 4G and 5G signal, but in some places the lack of it causes serious disruption.
articles.body:
Trudi King-Gunn works in a village with virtually no mobile phone signal.

She and the village's residents rely mostly on Wi-Fi and landlines to stay connected, but in a power cut that becomes problematic.

"The concern is when we need to call the emergency services," said Trudi.

Most areas of the UK now have access to 4G and 5G signal, but in some places the lack of it can cause serious disruption to people's lives.

Analysis by the consumer organisation Which? suggests the UK has the poorest mobile network quality in the G7 nations, while more than a third of mobile customers surveyed reported problems with poor signal.

BBC News has spoken to people in Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland and England to find out how the problem is affecting communities.

Eskdalemuir, where Trudi works, is a remote village in southern Scotland with about 250 residents.

"In the actual centre of Eskdalemuir, it is a blackspot," said Trudi, who works at the Eskdalemuir Community Hub.

There are concerns that with digital-only systems replacing analogue landlines, the villagers could be cut off in an emergency.

Power cuts are not uncommon in the area and not everyone has back-up batteries to keep their landlines operating.

"We have got a defibrillator and there have been a couple of issues when people have needed it and tried to ring the ambulance service," she said.

"Sometimes you can jump on [the hub's] Wi-Fi - if you are close enough."

She said back-up batteries were available but they would only keep landlines working for two or three hours.

The situation is even more frustrating, according to Trudi, because she knows there is good signal nearby.

"I live four miles down the road and I have perfect mobile signal but in [Eskdalemuir] there is just nothing," she added.

"There is no talk of any sort of change or mast going up or anything like that."

Villagers keep their fingers crossed that power cuts do not last long or that their back-up systems are sufficient.

BT said it offered a range of options in the event of a power cut, and that back-up power generators were being added to more sites.

In north Wales, the coastal town of Llandudno attracts millions of visitors every year.

But poor phone signal leaves traders struggling to process payments and visitors struggling to make calls.

"It affects us massively, especially with the number of businesses we have," said Paul Williams, general manager of Llandudno Pier.

"They all rely on the 5G signal to try and get the card transactions processed."

The problem was clear just moments after meeting kiosk owner Bella McBride, as one of her customers faced a long wait to pay by card.

"My card machine, for example, some days it can go down completely and not everybody carries cash," said Bella.

"It ranges from atrocious to completely useless," said Alan Heseldine, who runs a seafood kiosk on the pier.

"It's a major problem because I can't use the card machines to best effect. I can't make phone calls to suppliers, I have to wait until I go home or I can get Wi-Fi somewhere else.

"It's really difficult. It makes the job a lot harder than it needs to be."

Last year local councillors gave permission for new phone masts to be put up in the town, but the work is yet to be carried out.

The visual impact of any new masts has been raised as a concern, as Llandudno's Victorian seafront is a conservation area.

Tilly Adams-Mears, who was visiting Llandudno for the day to surprise her grandmother, said she was caught out by the lack of signal.

"I've been trying to contact my nan and you can't get hold of her at all. Honestly - there's no phone bars."

Meanwhile, 230 miles (370km) away on the opposite side of the UK, traders in the city of Ely, Cambridgeshire, face similar issues.

Tasnime Rotherham, 42, who runs a mobile catering business, said the notoriously bad signal in the city centre was affecting trade.

"Fifty percent of our payments are on card, so we need a decent signal," she said.

"I've lost a few sales because people have walked off and not realised their payment didn't go through.

"We now have trader Wi-Fi because the signal in the marketplace is like a black zone."

Ely does not have any phone masts in the city centre. Instead, they are dotted around the outskirts.

Telecommunications consultant Bob Driver said the size of Ely Cathedral also reduced connectivity.

"Because it's a historic town you don't want to see lots of base stations everywhere and people object to them, so planning permission is a problem," he added.

Tasnime has much better reception in her home village a couple of miles outside of Ely, which she described as "the middle of nowhere".

"I don't understand why we are OK [there]," she said.

Ely is looking at installing small booster cells on lamp-posts, which would cost less than a mast and not interfere with the city's landscape.

Mobile network operators cover the cost of these cells but they only boost the signal for about 150m (492ft). Mobile UK, which represents providers, said the cells were designed to complement masts, not replace them.

The roll-out of mobile services and infrastructure in the UK is led by private mobile network operators (MNOs).

According to the latest Ofcom data , 84% of the UK has good 4G coverage from all MNOs, while 96% of the UK has 4G coverage from at least one MNO.

Mobile UK said MNOs were investing billions across every UK nation to improve connectivity.

"We fully recognise the daily frustration poor signal causes for residents, high street traders, and rural communities trying to take card payments or stay connected."

But they said if governments wanted "world-class, reliable mobile connectivity" then planning systems needed to be "modernised", adding that "cutting this red tape is vital if operators are to deploy new sites".

The delivery of mobile infrastructure projects often overlaps with devolved powers, such as planning. But telecommunications is not devolved, meaning the UK government has primary responsibility for setting targets and policy.

The UK government said: "Fast, reliable digital infrastructure is fundamental to a growing economy. That's why we are working closely with industry to deliver our ambition of achieving 5G coverage across all populated areas of the UK by 2030.

"Through the Shared Rural Network, more than 95% of the UK's landmass is now within range of a 4G signal, one year ahead of the schedule, with the programme providing rural coverage to an area equivalent to almost 800,000 football pitches.

"Demand on mobile networks continues to grow, so we are looking at what more can be done to support investment and improve network performance over the long term through the Mobile Market Review."

In County Tyrone, Northern Ireland, where locals have previously described "complete blackspots" of phone signal, there are signs of improvement.

The expansion of mobile network infrastructure has faced the challenge of strict planning laws and, in recent years, frequent arson attacks linked to online conspiracy theories.

The Northern Ireland Executive launched a Mobile Action Plan in 2020 with the aim of working with MNOs to identify issues and "support rollout and expansion".

Catháir Brady, who works at a theatre in the town of Coalisland, said the 5G coverage had subsequently improved and was now "reliable enough", whereas before it could "get worse by moving even a few feet".

However, he said 5G coverage in the neighbouring town of Clonoe, where he lives, remained "awful".

A few miles away in Stewartstown, Joanne Sinclair said recent improvements to 4G and 5G coverage had been hugely beneficial to her family's hardware store.

"Many different networks work," said Joanne, while previously only a very small number of networks received 5G coverage in the area, and these were often patchy.

She said the improvements had come in the last five years and the improved 4G and 5G coverage was useful for processing payments and making calls.

"I make a lot of business phone calls off my mobile," she said, adding that before the improvements, staff would have to stand in a specific part of the office just to make a call.

Additional reporting by Rosie Mercer and Ema Sabljak

articles.title: US Supreme Court denies Christa Pike's last-ditch bid to halt execution
articles.summary: Tennessee inmate Christa Pike has been awaiting execution since her 1996 murder conviction.
articles.body:
The US Supreme Court has declined to stop the execution of Tennessee inmate Christa Pike on the eve of the date appointed for her death by lethal injection.

Pike, 50, has been awaiting execution since she was convicted and sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of a teenage classmate.

Hoping for a last-minute reprieve, her attorneys filed a petition with the high court ahead of her scheduled execution on Wednesday morning.

But after the high court's decision to deny that request, Pike will be the first woman to be executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Only 18 women have been executed in the US since the 1970s, compared to 1,663 men.

On Monday, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee denied a request for clemency from Pike, saying he would not intervene in her planned execution.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend beat, tortured and murdered Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old they met at a job training camp for troubled teens.

She is due to be executed at 11:00 EDT (15:00 GMT) on Wednesday at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville.

articles.title: Canadian broadcaster reportedly pulled after recording anti-Israel protest outside service
articles.summary: Newsreader Neil Herland's viral video of an anti-Israel protest outside a Toronto synagogue service on Yom Kippur reportedly led CBC to pull him off-air.
articles.body: Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) newsreader Neil Herland was reportedly pulled off the air and faced an internal investigation after posting a video of an anti-Israel protest outside a synagogue service last week. Herland documented himself attempting to enter a service held by The Song Shul at the Meridian Arts Centre that was protested by about two dozen demonstrators holding signs and noisemakers while chanting, "Free, Free Palestine." "I'm a journalist. And I happen to be Jewish. On Yom Kippur I went to a synagogue service in Toronto and was met by protesters trying to taunt and intimidate me from entering the building," Herland wrote on X. ANTI-ISRAEL AGITATORS CLASH WITH NYPD OFFICERS NEAR SYNAGOGUE In the video, a man shouted "Zionist alert" as Herland approached the building, and Herland was accosted by a man shouting, "You're going to hell" for attending the service, which featured Israeli diplomat and former Benjamin Netanyahu advisor Mark Regev as a speaker. In follow-up comments, Herland emphasized his growing concerns that Canada itself may no longer be safe for Jewish people. "My late father was an Austrian Jew who survived the Holocaust in Romania. And came to Canada as a refugee. This year I got an Austrian passport, in case Canada becomes unsafe for me as a Jew. I fear that moment is approaching, here in Canada and elsewhere," Herland wrote. "Jewish Canadians are living in a parallel world," he added. "Where police stand guard with guns outside synagogues. And Jewish schools, religious sites and businesses are targeted with bullets. And most Canadians have no awareness or understanding." CANADA'S CARNEY PLEDGES ACTION ON ANTISEMITISM AMID BACKLASH OVER NEW ANTI-HATE COUNCIL MEMBERS The video has since received 3.8 million views. After Herland posted his comments, The Toronto Sun reported Thursday that the veteran journalist was pulled from his on-air job and informed that he would be investigated based on complaints made to the company. Herland himself has not posted anything from his X account since Friday. Though it is unclear what complaints could have led to this decision, the organization Canadians for Justice and Peace in the Middle East (CJPME) encouraged followers on X to send in complaints, claiming that Herland was purposefully misleading people about the situation. "On September 21, @CBC National Radio News Reader @NEWSneil Neil Herland posted on X that was 'met by [pro-Palestine] protesters trying to taunt and intimidate [him] from entering [a synagogue service in Toronto].' He shared an accompanying video of Palestine solidarity protesters." "However, Herland was on his way to the Meridian Arts Centre, not a synogogue, to see Mark Regev. Regev was not merely a teacher and former Israeli ambassador, but served in multiple high-ranking positions in the Israeli government, including as the Prime Minister’s Senior Advisor for Foreign Affairs and International Communications and the International Spokesperson for the Prime Minister’s Office," the CJPME's post read. CBC TELLS JOURNALISTS NOT TO CALL 9/11 ‘TERRORIST ATTACKS’ IN INTERNAL GUIDANCE The post continued, "The reality is that Herland was telling a demonstrable lie to defame pro-Palestine activists. Join us in writing to the Values and Ethics Commissioner for CBC/Radio-Canada, Sherry Perreault, to express serious concerns about apparent ethics violations by Neil Herland." When reached for comment, CBC spokesperson Chuck Thompson told Fox News Digital that CBC would not comment on the matter but claimed that reporting has been filled with "errors and mischaracterizations." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Fully respecting the privacy rights of our employees, we don’t comment on internal matters. That said, we are aware of reporting on this matter which has errors and mischaracterizations but we can't get into the specifics given the confidentiality of the situation," Thompson said.

articles.title: CMLL talents look to increase popularity among American pro wrestling fans with latest opportunity
articles.summary: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre's AEW partnership now lets U.S. fans stream CMLL shows on MyAEW, solving the long-standing access problem for Lucha Libre.
articles.body: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) is one of the most historic pro wrestling promotions on the planet. The company was founded in 1933 and continues to honor Lucha Libre style wrestling to this day. As pro wrestling’s popularity has increased dramatically over the years, CMLL has had the need to get more eyeballs on its product. Among the steps the company has taken, CMLL partnered with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) to feature its superstars on its programming. The partnership has allowed CMLL legends like Místico to appear at AEW and Ring of Honor shows while still being the generational figure that he is in Mexico. The same has held true for a lot of CMLL talent. The next step was to find a footing in the United States. With immense potential, CMLL held its first solo event in Las Vegas as part of Slam Fest during WrestleMania weekend. The action-packed event saw the likes of Blue Panther, Ultimo Guerrero, Persephone, Tessa Blanchard, Místico, Hechicero, Templario, Angel de Oro and others showcase their talent. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE Passionate pro wrestling fans could easily get hooked on the athleticism and storytelling that CMLL brings in the ring. But what about watching it at home? Where can the average pro wrestling fan watch incredible Lucha Libre? MyAEW was launched with that concept in mind – giving fans access to events they normally wouldn’t be able to find elsewhere. CMLL’s New Japan Pro-Wrestling Fantastica Mania Mexico 2026 was added to the event schedule. Several more shows were added to the docket after that, including the company’s anniversary event which was held back on Sept. 18. "This is a huge deal," CMLL Mexican national champion Thunder Rosa told OutKick Dropkick in a recent interview. "A lot of people have been asking for a long time, how can they watch CMLL, right? And I think right now CMLL is at a point in where it's known globally. I mean, it's known globally like people every time that they come to Mexico City, they come to Arena, México to experience what Lucha Libre is. But it's always been like this dark area and like, Where can I watch this? And they were like you can go on YouTube. CMLL has had a subscription based activity with YouTube and where you can watch all the CMLL stuff in there but now they partner with AEW with this big partnership that we have had on this almost for two years and now people in America, if you have access to MyAEW.com you can watch the shows. "It excites me because as someone who works in both companies, now I can tell people, if you have MyAEW.com now you can watch CMLL and I hope that a lot of the other programming from CMLL is there too because there's been fantastic matches in the last I want to say last year. CMLL just in general has the best wrestling in the world. Just like AEW where the best wrestle, CMLL is we're the best wrestle." Miguel Castro wears many hats for CMLL. But most who tune into the English-speaking commentary will hear his voice on the broadcast. Castro said that while AEW has given CMLL as platform to showcase the best it has to offer, trying to carve out an audience and build a brand in the United States is a challenge in and of itself. "Mostly brand recognition," Castro told OutKick Dropkick when asked what were some of the obstacles in the way of growth in the U.S. "I believe that our talents’ work speaks for itself. Anyone that enjoys wrestling, even if you like it by 5% compared to a fan, you will enjoy a CMLL show. It's not all about the drama and the storytelling, and that, I think that's what has made such a good connection with AEW and with New Japan Pro-Wrestling, we're heavily focused on the sports. It'll make you gasp, it will make you scream, you'll have fun, and then you're gonna want to know more." Castro added that CMLL has very little, if at all, advertising budget and still sells out Arena México for its shows. He credited AEW for giving CMLL a showcase for its talent, brand and helping create stars in the U.S. If Místico is on the card in an AEW or Ring of Honor show, fans will sing his entrance music "Me Muero." "I would love to increase the pay-per-view numbers 10 times on MyAEW and I know that's going to happen as they also grow their base in the platform," he said. "My main focus right now would be to have a media deal in the States. And ideally not in Univision or Telemundo. Like I don't want it to be part of a TV station just because it's Mexican. "But we just started three months ago with Fox Sports in Mexico and I can tell you that we're getting about a million pairs of eyeballs every month. articles.title: WOW champion Santana Garrett talks choosing pro wrestling over teaching, Jeanie Buss in the ring and more
articles.summary: Santana Garrett reveals the childhood dream that led her to become a two-time WOW World Championship holder after 18 years in pro wrestling.
articles.body: The pro wrestling world is incredibly vast. Champions sit on top of every promotion and sometimes, it’s hard to keep track of who is the best of the best throughout the sport. Santana Garrett has announced her presence with authority with the Women of Wrestling (WOW). Garrett has appeared in WWE, All Elite Wrestling and Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) in her career and has found success at WOW. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE She is one of five WOW superstars who have held the WOW World Championship twice. No wrestler who has ever competed in the promotion has won the belt more than that. Garrett, a second-generation pro wrestler, opened up about her career with OutKick Dropkick recently. She said she knew her life was going to take her down one of three paths – to the ring, to the weather desk or to the classroom. "I've been in the industry my entire life. I'm a second generation wrestler. My father was a wrestler on the independent scene. I grew up as a fan watching it with him, going to shows. So, just kind of always being around it," she said. "When I was a little girl, I knew that I wanted to be a weather girl or a professional wrestler or an elementary art teacher. So, I took the route of professional wrestling and it's been an incredible journey. "It has taken me all over the world. Along the way, there's been obstacles, ups and downs, like anything, but I wouldn't change a thing. It's been it's been so nice. And I just recently won the WOW World Championship, which I'm so proud of. I won it once before, but it's been a very long time and a lot has changed. You can imagine 18 years, you evolve and this time it just feels so different and I love it." Garrett said she grew up watching the likes of "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, Trish Stratus and Lita and began training in her grandfather’s backyard in Ocala, Florida. She said from her first real workout in St. Louis, she knew she could make a career out of pro wrestling. She won her first title in 2016 when she defeated Jungle Grrrl and The Beverley Hills Babe. She pinned The Beverley Hills Babe in the triple-threat match. The title was vacated more than 740 days later after Garrett and Jungle Grrrl had both pinned Tessa Blanchard. Garrett lost the title then only to regain it years later against Penelope Pink. Now, Garrett said she’s more than ready to be the face of WOW. "It feels incredible," she told OutKick Dropkick. articles.title: Motorists in Wales face fines of up to £150 for idling
articles.summary: The previous punishment for idling was £20 and had not changed since its introduction in 2003.
articles.body:
Drivers in Wales who leave their vehicle engine running while parked will face fines of up to £150 from Wednesday.

The change is part of a new measure by the Welsh government to try to reduce harmful pollution and to protect children's health.

The previous punishment for idling, as it is known, was £20 but that has now been raised to anywhere from £75 to £150, depending on circumstances.

The Welsh government said it hoped the increase will "change the habits of people who are polluting communities".

Llyr Gruffydd, cabinet minister for rural resilience and sustainability, said the £20 fixed fine for idling was "insufficient", and not being used "in the way everyone might envision it".

Increasing the fee that is available for local authorities to penalise drivers will be a "stronger deterrent", he added.

"We really do feel we need to step up here, clamp down on this as a problem and make sure we protect people's health and generally it will make communities a better place to live in."

Gruffydd said he hoped the higher range of fines will "change the habits of people who are polluting communities and are putting children and vulnerable people's health at risk".

Anna, who was collecting her children from Treganna school in Cardiff, welcomed the new measure.

She lives close to the school and said it got "really, really busy because cars are everywhere around here".

"When we actually want to leave here, to go somewhere, we can't during these hours," she said, adding it once took her 45 minutes to get down the road.

"For us it's kind of good because it will stop a lot of these cars from parking here."

Chiara Rinaldi, another parent, said: "I think they probably have a good principle behind them but I think the reality is nobody is going to enforce them.

"School runs are chaotic as it is but you're never going to get the police out here are you enforcing fines.

"It's a great idea but never going to happen."

One parent who frequently collects her children from school on foot is Wendy Vernon-Fulook, and she believes the higher fine is a "good thing".

"You shouldn't be leaving the car running, obviously it's not good for the environment and it might stop people from doing it.

"It might not, people might keep doing it unfortunately, but we're trying to encourage people to walk as much as possible, so it can only be a good thing."

But Rhiannon Simmonds said: "I'm not sure I agree with it, if a mandatory solution is the way to go about it, but I completely appreciate the logic of what they're trying to do for sure."

Under rule 123 of the Highway Code, drivers must not leave a parked vehicle unattended with the engine running or leave a vehicle engine running unnecessarily while that vehicle is stationary on a public road.

Areas outside schools have been identified as high risk sites where emissions pose particular concerns.

Hospitals, GP surgeries, care homes and other healthcare facilities are also identified as high risk locations.

Professor Isabel Oliver, chief medical officer for Wales, said air pollution was a serious public health issue that contributed to a range of conditions including heart and lung disease.

"Children, older people and those with existing health conditions are particularly vulnerable to its effects," she said.

"Idling may seem like a small, everyday habit, but it adds up.

"Every time an engine is switched off rather than left running, we reduce the amount of harmful pollution in the air we all breathe, particularly around schools, hospitals and other places where vulnerable people spend time."

This new measure comes into force following a vote at the Senedd in March.

MSs passed the new rules, with 37 politicians voting for and 12 against. There were no abstentions.

articles.title: Was Iran behind a ‘terror plot’ targeting U.S. forces in Britain?
articles.summary: A transatlantic mystery is capturing attention in the U.S. and Britain. The central question is whether Iran was behind some kind of plot to target a British air base that is vital to the U.S. Air Force (USAF). Alternatively, was the initial speculation about an incident that has seen five men arrested, and then released…
articles.body:
A transatlantic mystery is capturing attention in the U.S. and Britain.

The central question is whether Iran was behind some kind of plot to target a British air base that is vital to the U.S. Air Force (USAF).

Alternatively, was the initial speculation about an incident that has seen five men arrested, and then released on police bail, overhyped?

President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have weighed in on the matter, as have senior figures in British politics and policing.

But the whole matter has become more and more shadowy, and questions proliferate.

Here’s a guide to where things stand on Tuesday evening, U.S time.

In the early hours of Sunday morning, British time, five men were arrested close to RAF Fairford, an air base about 90 miles west of London in the county of Gloucestershire.

The men had three white vans. The vans have been widely reported to carry the logos and details of a fuel company. But the markings were apparently counterfeit, and the men have no connection to the real company.

Initially, the alarm was said to have been raised by a farmer who was startled to see men wearing ski masks in the dead of night, and the three vans oddly arrayed.

However, in a Tuesday update, the UK’s head of National Counter-Terrorism Policing, Laurence Taylor, suggested the call was just one factor amid “a range of information received.”

The arrests sparked instant speculation that there was a link to the U.S. war on Iran.

In March, then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer gave permission for the base to be used by U.S. planes headed to Iran, with the proviso that this applied only to “defensive” missions, such as targeting Iranian military facilities.

The USAF’s 501st Combat Support Wing says on its website that Fairford is “home to the 501st Combat Support Wing Headquarters and the 420th Air Base Squadron and serves as the preferred bomber forward operating location in Europe for USAF Global Strike Command.”

The use of bases for the U.S. war on Iran is controversial in Britain, where both Trump and the war are unpopular.

What’s happened since the initial arrests?

When news of the arrests first broke, the idea that a “terror plot” had been uncovered commanded the headlines.

This could yet prove to be true. And it isn’t just conjecture out of thin air, either. In July, Iran had warned that any base “used for aggression against Iranian territory” would be considered a “legitimate target.”

But things now seem far more complicated.

The men were initially arrested on suspicion of explosives offenses. But Taylor, the British counter-terrorism chief, confirmed on Tuesday that no explosives had been found in the three vans, though “a quantity of petrol was recovered.”

It has been widely reported in the British media that the five men are all UK nationals in their early-to-mid 20s who live in London. This does not preclude a link to Iran, of course, but it seems a bit incongruous with the “terror plot” thesis.

Adding to the perplexity is the British police’s decision to release the men on bail. It’s near-certain that bail would have been refused if the men were seen as a present danger to the public or to national security.

Taylor on Tuesday said the men must “adhere to strict conditions” while on bail and emphasized the investigation is continuing.

He added, regarding the granting of bail, “I understand why this development will have come as a surprise to many, but I’d like to reiterate that it was an investigative decision, and one which is grounded in experience and careful consideration of policing powers.”

In the past few hours, there has been a new, bizarre wrinkle: The Times of London reported on Tuesday evening, UK time, that the first call alerting authorities had actually come from one of the suspects.

The newspaper said one of the men called 999 — the British equivalent of the 911 emergency line — almost one hour before the call from the farmer.

The Times is a well-regarded news organization but nobody is sure what to make of this new detail.

What’s the view from the Trump administration?

The President is among those startled by the decision to release the five men on bail.

On Monday, Trump said he was “surprised” by the move. “I would have said don’t let them have bail,” he told reporters in the Oval Office. “I wouldn’t have done that.”

Pushed on whether Iran was behind the episode, Trump offered an enigmatic answer: “I know the answer. I can be very specific. But I’d rather not say.”

Rubio, speaking with Fox News on Monday evening, called the events at RAF Fairford “a very serious situation” and added that it was “one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor.”

The Trump and Rubio comments are clearly suggestive of Iranian involvement. While Trump often shoots from the hip, it is less likely that Rubio is making such a claim without some supporting evidence. But it’s not clear so far what that evidence might be.

Some confusion also surrounds comments Trump made at an earlier stage, soon after the arrests, when he said of the men, “We had them under view for a long time, and we got them.”

British media have cited anonymous sources suggesting this may be inaccurate. It’s also possible that what Trump said was correct but that British authorities had wanted to keep surveillance or even the use of informants under wraps.

The Iranian embassy in London has emphatically denied that the Islamic Republic is behind the incident.

In a Monday social media post , the embassy called suggestions of a link “unfounded and malicious speculations.”

The embassy also complained that such claims “will serve no purpose other than to fuel Iranophobia propaganda in the UK.”

Everyone is trying to square the apparent contradictions.

On one hand, there is the arrest of a group of men behaving suspiciously near a base used by U.S. forces — a location that Iran plainly considers a legitimate target.

On the other hand, there’s the lack of explosives, the decision to bail the men, and the fact that they have not been charged. There is no actual proof of wrongdoing as of Tuesday evening and the men are entitled to the presumption of innocence even if they were to be charged.

Among those who believe something nefarious was going on, the least grave suggestion is that the men could have been fuel thieves with no political motivation at all. But anonymous sources quoted in the UK media appeared to be dampening that speculation on Tuesday.

One theory that has got more traction is that the men could have been conducting a “dry run” aimed at testing security. If that were the case, could the emergency call from the suspect have been intended to gauge police reaction times? But, if it was, why would the men have let themselves get arrested rather than fleeing before police arrived?

There has been talk in British security circles of Iran using proxies — often low-level criminals paid to carry out basic tasks. And it’s also possible that the men were engaging in a stunt to sow confusion and fear.

It’s worth reiterating it’s also possible the five men are innocent of any crime at all.

For now, the case is captivating in part because nobody knows.
